DesignProposal: Replace single global advisory lock hashtext('eap_outbox_lock') with 1,024 striped shard locks.

DeadlockEvaluation.SingleAccountTransactions: Deadlock-free: each transaction touches only one account and acquires only one shard lock.
DeadlockEvaluation.MultiAccountTransactions: Deadlock vulnerable: if Transaction 1 updates Account A (Shard 1) then Account B (Shard 2), while Transaction 2 updates Account B (Shard 2) then Account A (Shard 1), an unresolvable PostgreSQL deadlock occurs.
DeadlockEvaluation.DeadlockAvoidanceRule: Multi-account transactions MUST sort distinct shard IDs in strict ascending order and acquire locks in that sequence.

SequenceGapAnomaly.ProblemDescription: In PostgreSQL, BIGSERIAL sequences are non-transactional: sequence values are incremented immediately upon nextval() before transaction commit. If Transactions T1 and T2 run concurrently on different shard locks, T1 may receive seq_id=100 and T2 may receive seq_id=101. If T2 commits while T1 is still in flight, seq_id=101 becomes visible while seq_id=100 is uncommitted.
SequenceGapAnomaly.GlobalWatermarkFailure: If an outbox poller queries `WHERE seq_id > @lastSeq ORDER BY seq_id` and advances @lastSeq to 101, it advances past 100. When T1 subsequently commits seq_id=100, the poller will NEVER see it because 100 <= 101. That mutation is permanently lost from the cache!
SequenceGapAnomaly.WhySingleGlobalLockWasUsed: The single global advisory lock serializes commits so that seq_id generation order strictly matches transaction commit order, eliminating sequence gaps at the cost of capping throughput at ~370 writes/second.

FeasibleArchitecturesForHighThroughput.Name: Per-Shard Outbox Queues
FeasibleArchitecturesForHighThroughput.Description: Maintain 1,024 separate outbox queues/sequences. Each shard maintains its own independent watermark. Eliminates global lock contention without gap anomalies.

FeasibleArchitecturesForHighThroughput.Name: PostgreSQL Logical Replication / WAL Decoding
FeasibleArchitecturesForHighThroughput.Description: Use PostgreSQL logical decoding (test_decoding or pgoutput) to stream committed transactions from WAL. Guarantees gap-free commit-order delivery without application locks.

FeasibleArchitecturesForHighThroughput.Name: Sliding Window / Commit Confirmation Watermark
FeasibleArchitecturesForHighThroughput.Description: Track individual committed seq_ids using a sliding bitmap window, only advancing the contiguous high-watermark when all lower sequence numbers have committed or timed out.
